headline: Majors hold above 200-day lines while shorts absorb liquidations; whale inflows to exchanges over 48 hours clash with week-old outflow pattern.
paragraphs: All seven majors trade above their 200-day moving averages, and five carry golden crosses (BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP absent the cross, BNB, with DOGE and ADA below the line entirely). The regime is structurally up, but the momentum picture tells a different story. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and XRP all show MACD below signal, meaning the recent advance has lost upside thrust. RSI values cluster between 49 and 60, neutral to slightly overbought but nowhere extreme: BTC at 54.4, ETH at 59.9, SOL at 55.1. The tension is clear: the trend is up, but the accelerant is off. A glance at the intraday moves reinforces this: Bitcoin down 0.2% on the day after a 5.1% drop over the week, yet up 22.8% on the month. Ethereum down 1.4% today and down 0.7% over seven days, but up 35.1% in 30 days. The same rhythm holds across Solana, XRP, and BNB. ADA and DOGE remain wounded, the former up 0.1% today but down 6.1% over the week and down 71.1% and 77.7% from their 12-month highs respectively. What the reader should register: the bulk of the rally is in the books already; today and this week are consolidation or pullback, not extension.

Funding remains positive across the majors but not hot. Bitcoin perpetuals pay 0.55% over eight hours, annualizing to 6.0% on OKX, with Ethereum at 0.45% (5.0% annual). These are ordinary carry, not crowded. Solana flipped negative at minus 0.15% per eight hours (minus 1.6% annual), a signal that long positions are no longer paying a premium. Open interest is substantial, Bitcoin holding 2.19 billion USD and Ethereum 1.62 billion, but the real finding lives in the liquidation tape over the past hour to eight hours. Bitcoin saw 100 liquidations with 527,940 USD in shorts wiped versus 12,337 USD in longs: a 42-to-1 ratio. Ethereum the same: 100 liquidations, 429,727 USD in shorts, zero in longs. Solana reversed the picture hard, with 804,291 USD in long liquidations against 14,470 in shorts over six hours, the only major where longs are getting flushed. XRP and DOGE saw longs liquidated heavily (527,009 and 525,542 USD respectively) with shorts largely spared. The long-short ratios across BTC (1.74), ETH (1.66), and especially XRP (2.89) and DOGE (4.54) confirm the positioning: retail and leveraged longs are stacked, Solana is the outlier where the other side got cornered.

Whale flows over the past 48 hours paint a narrative of distribution into exchanges: 226,996,468 USD net moved onto exchanges, with Bitcoin accounting for the entire figure (469.8 million in, 242.8 million out, net 227 million in). The five-day ETF picture splits the story: Bitcoin spot ETFs saw a 13.2 million USD outflow on September 11, extending a four-day pattern of same-direction outflows totaling 288.1 million USD over five sessions. Ethereum spot ETFs ran the opposite play: 216.4 million USD in on the same day, with a cumulative five-session inflow of 222.8 million. The crypto tape shows whales dumping into Coinbase and other major venues while traditional finance (via ETF channels) took a Bitcoin exit and scooped Ethereum. Stablecoin float sits at 310.2 billion USD, up 1.35% over 30 days, dry powder unchanged. The weekly whale flow summary shows the rhythm: week ending August 23, 1,062 million USD onto exchanges, week ending August 30, 659 million onto exchanges, then a break week ending September 6 with 494 million OFF exchanges (the only recent respite), followed immediately by 827 million back onto exchanges in the week ending September 13. The thesis: large holders are liquidating into the rally, rebalancing or taking profit, while smaller accumulators via ETF channels show selective demand.

Sentiment sits at 61 (Greed), in the top half of its 30-day range of 31 to 74. The crowd is confident but not euphoric, appropriate to the data: prices up a month but down a week, funding ordinary, momentum flat, and the big money heading for exits. The contradiction is mild but real. Fear and Greed does not lead the tape; it lags it. A greed reading with Bitcoin down 5.1% over seven days and shorts getting liquidated at 40-to-1 ratios while whales fence into exchanges is a gauge that is catching up to what happened, not forecasting what comes next.

Total market cap fell 4.03% on the day to 2.629 trillion USD, with Bitcoin dominance steady at 58.9%. The altcoin complex weakened more than Bitcoin itself, a sign of rotation or risk-off within crypto. FIL led gainers at 12.87%, while ETHFI cratered 14.39%, a divergence that suggests event-driven moves rather than macro positioning. Bitcoin network difficulty is set to climb 4.6% at retarget (847 blocks remain), in step with a market that has held its footing despite recent pressure.

Watch three conditions: (1) whether BTC and ETH MACD lines cross back above signal while prices hold the 200-day (a real upside restart), (2) the next ETF flow window, specifically whether Bitcoin inflows resume or the five-session outflow persists (a tell on institutional conviction), and (3) whether whale flows reverse off exchanges over the next 48 hours (a sign that selling pressure has exhausted itself). Solana's inverted liquidation pattern (longs getting hit while shorts survive) bears watching as a potential leading indicator of momentum exhaustion in the altcoin space.
